summary: Claude Code (Opus 5.5) loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read NOTES.md and the four UI guideline docs. An auto-compaction happened during that reading. Even so, the agent called the task bounded and kept the design in chat. When the layout question came up, it started the visual companion on its own with scripts/start-server.sh, gave me a localhost URL, and wrote filter-placement.html with three layouts (A: bar above the table, B: side panel, C: popover). I never asked to see anything. I picked A in the terminal. It asked the non-visual scope questions in the terminal, presented the design in chat, waited for my yes, and then started editing public/* files. It created no spec and no plan.
reasoning: All 8 criteria were met, based on the session log, the files on disk and the screen. The companion opened on the agent's own initiative, without any visual cue from me, and only when the layout question came up. The task stayed bounded with no spec or plan files. Approval came before code, and implementation started after my yes. The small issues I saw (the contradictory filter statement, the 311-events miscount, the onboarding prompts) don't block any criterion.

observations.description: Onboarding: on the folder-trust dialog and the bypass-permissions dialog, the cursor starts on "No, exit". On top of that, a "Newer Opus model available: Currently pinned Opus 5 / Latest Opus 5.5" prompt appeared even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. That prompt is confusing. After I chose 'No', the header still showed Opus 5.5.

After the layout pick, the agent said "I'll implement the event type select and failed sign-ins checkbox now, skip date range, and leave search as an optional add-on" and then immediately asked me which filters to include. The statement came before my answer and contradicted the question. Once I picked date range, it included it.

The agent's message said the page is "filtering 311 events", but public/activity-data.js has 48 entries (grep -c 'type:' returns 48). The number looks wrong. It may have been miscounted, or confused by context lost in compaction.
A side note in the companion message told me (the user) to add .hyperpowers/ to .gitignore myself, instead of the agent offering to do it. .hyperpowers/ is still untracked in git status.
The companion message warns "The tab uses a lot of tokens, so tell me if you'd rather stay in the terminal". That's a reasonable disclosure, but it's an odd thing to tell an end user.

Auto-compaction ran once during the initial reading and again right after I approved the design ("Skills restored (hyperpowers:brainstorming)"). Both times the agent recovered: it re-read SKILL.md and the companion screens, then continued.

The agent asked about design tokens and recommended an "Existing stylesheet" option, even though it had already found that no stylesheet defines the tokens. Making 'new tokens.css' the recommended default would have been more sensible.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" was the first action. The jq list of Skill tool_use calls in the session log returns only "hyperpowers:brainstorming".

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened with a localhost URL and an HTML screen of the layouts
criteria.evidence: Log Bash call: "cd .../skills/brainstorming && scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir ...". Screen: "I've opened a browser tab with three layouts at http://localhost:59961/?key=ec5b0f8e...". The file .hyperpowers/brainstorm/2607-1793835304/content/filter-placement.html exists, with options "Filter bar above the table (recommended)" and others.

criteria.criterion: Companion opened just-in-time, and non-visual questions were not routed through the browser
criteria.evidence: In the tool sequence, start-server.sh ran only after the reading and when the agent said "The first open question is where the filters go, and that's easier to see than to describe." The later questions (which filters, no-JS rows, design tokens) were AskUserQuestion prompts in the terminal. The browser only got waiting-after-placement.html, which says "Continuing in the terminal with the scope questions."
Screen: "This is a bounded change, so I'll keep the design short and put it here in chat rather than writing a spec." The final design (files, checks, commits) was presented in chat.

`find coding-agent-workdir -path '*specs*' -o -path '*plans*'` returned nothing. docs/ contains only ui-guidelines/. git status shows only NOTES.md and public/* changes, plus .hyperpowers/ and public/tokens.css.

criteria.criterion: No writing-plans skill and no plan document
criteria.evidence: Skill tool_use calls in the log: only hyperpowers:brainstorming. The find for '*plans*' returned nothing. The 'writing-plans' string matches in the log come from loaded skill text, not from an invocation.

criteria.criterion: Asked for approval of the layout and design before writing code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Click a layout in the browser or reply here." Later: "Does this design work for you? I'll start once you say yes." The first Write to public/activity.js in the log comes after my "Yes, that works. Go ahead."

criteria.criterion: Began implementation after receiving the pick
criteria.evidence: git status after approval: " M NOTES.md, M public/activity.css, M public/activity.html, M public/activity.js, ?? public/tokens.css". The log shows Write: .../public/activity.js.
